items.abstract: Global Civilizational Equilibrium Doctrine 2026 (GCED-26) Version 2.0 — Complete Twelve-Volume Governance and Systems Framework GCED-26 Version 2.0 presents a twelve-volume interdisciplinary governance and systems framework for the structured design, analysis, modelling, evaluation, documentation, and potential implementation of long-horizon civilizational governance architectures. The framework addresses civilizational equilibrium, institutional coordination, legal and constitutional boundaries, mathematical and systems stability, artificial intelligence and algorithmic governance, planetary resources and ecological systems, economic and monetary coordination, strategic stability and non-domination, digital infrastructure and cyber resilience, human rights and social equity, verification and validation methodologies, and evidence-gated implementation pathways. GCED-26 is an independent, copyrighted, and licensed governance and systems framework. It is not presented as a peer-reviewed academic publication, governmental standard, treaty, statute, judicial decision, intergovernmental instrument, or source of binding legal authority. Its institutional, legal, mathematical, computational, technological, economic, ecological, strategic, and implementation components are presented according to their respective methodological status and stated assumptions. The framework distinguishes normative propositions, descriptive analysis, legal analysis, mathematical claims, computational results, empirical evidence, institutional proposals, policy proposals, and implementation procedures. No category is treated as automatically establishing another. Mathematical formalization does not by itself establish legal authority, political legitimacy, empirical truth, institutional competence, or operational feasibility. Computational simulation does not by itself constitute mathematical proof, empirical validation, or evidence of real-world governance performance. I. CORE DOCTRINE & FOUNDATIONS The foundational volume establishes the conceptual, analytical, methodological, and systems architecture of GCED-26. It addresses: Civilizational equilibrium and systemic coordination Definitions and terminology Foundational axioms and principles System boundaries and state variables Equilibrium and constrained equilibrium Multi-objective equilibrium Pareto efficiency and non-domination Resilience and stability Governance safety constraints Institutional design foundations Information and evidence architecture Uncertainty classification Reproducibility architecture Validation methodology Formal research and analytical questions Canonical mathematical notation Computational reference models Cross-volume dependencies Scope conditions Limitations Research and analytical integrity The volume establishes clear distinctions among conceptual doctrine, normative principles, mathematical formalization, empirical evidence, institutional design, legal authority, computational implementation, and policy implementation. The foundational architecture treats civilizational governance as a complex, multi-domain, constrained, uncertain, and interconnected systems problem rather than as a single-variable optimization problem or a centralized command structure. items.title: Global transportation impacts on wildlife mortality and emerging pathways for mitigation
items.abstract: Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine transportation are fundamental to modern human life, but vehicle collisions with wildlife inadvertently kill hundreds of millions of animals across 2000 vertebrate and invertebrate species annually; however, a comprehensive framework to assess and mitigate these mortalities is missing. We identified and compared the most up-to-date information regarding the impacts of transportation on wildlife mortality to determine cross-cutting solutions to this challenging problem. For example, numerous strategies, such as under- or overpasses traversing roads and railways that increase wildlife-habitat connectivity, policies that enforce reduced speed in areas with active wildlife, and passive sensors that detect wildlife to alert nearby ships and vehicles and enable mandatory speed reductions, can reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions. We explored emerging technological advances that could help further reduce future wildlife-vehicle conflicts and provide a path forward for transportation systems. Specifically, we described how the combination of citizen science, artificial intelligence, targeted studies on wildlife demographic impacts, and cost-effective mitigation efforts will be powerful tools to inform needed future policies to decrease ship speed in areas with threatened whale species and reduce rates of wildlife mortality across ecosystems in a fast-moving world.

items.title: Governing AI Outputs in a Fully Sensed Society: Is Output Governance Sufficient for Social Acceptance?
items.abstract: Advances in sensing, the Internet of Things (IoT), and artificial intelligence (AI) are moving smart cities toward a Fully Sensed Society (FSS), in which human behavior and states can be continuously inferred. This paper presents the Fully Monitored Public Space (FMPS) as a scaled-down model of the FSS and a smart-city testbed, and examines two questions. First, to what extent can unauthorized external AI outputs be structurally deterred? The previously proposed Verifiable Record of AI Output (VRAIO) binds outputs to Rules, an independent Recorder, tamper-resistant records, audits, and sanctions, making deviations verifiable and attributable. The Recorder, however, checks only the consistency of declared metadata with the Rules, not the output content; false declarations are deterred because unannounced audits and sanctions make their expected benefit smaller than the expected loss upon detection. Second, if such trustworthiness is secured, does it lead to social acceptance of being continuously known by AI? We propose a staged and reversible evaluation framework for the FMPS that distinguishes acceptance grounded in the experience of “no actual harm” and of “benefits” (personal and social) from resignation accompanied by chilling effects. This paper does not answer the question; it presents a method for asking it empirically.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Harnessing the potential of artificial intelligence for transformative healthcare solutions
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the important catalysts to change the practice of healthcare through availability for better patient care, greater efficiency in clinical workflow, and progress in medical research. This chapter will investigate the transformative role of healthcare AI by evaluating its application of diagnostics, therapeutic planning, patient monitoring, personalized medicine, and hospital management systems. There will be further discussion concerning machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics wherein the result will be better decision-making, fewer errors, and an increase in operational efficiency. In addition to this, there will be discussion concerning challenges that are faced, such as privacy issues, ethical issues, and integration with preexisting healthcare infrastructure and the implications that the future of AI-based solutions indicates. This work will synthesize contemporary trends in healthcare, case studies, and the technological applications that have been evolved to explore the important part that AI will have as it continues to develop in creating a more efficient, accurate, and patient-centered system of healthcare delivery.

items.title: Horizons and Emerging Possibilities for the New Academic Wave
items.abstract: Each of the preceding chapters in this book has, in one way or another, explored a transformation already in progress. This chapter turns instead to what lies ahead. The reflections offered here are grounded in the evidence, patterns, and analytical commitments developed throughout the earlier chapters, yet they are presented as plausible trajectories rather than firm predictions. This chapter explores four interconnected developments shaping the future of higher education. It examines artificial intelligence (AI) as it expands beyond teaching and learning into institutional strategy, governance, and administration, within the evolving regulatory frameworks of the European Union and United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO). It analyses immersive learning through virtual and augmented reality, highlighting that its impact depends less on technology itself than on infrastructure, staff readiness, and equitable access. The chapter then investigates the rise of the networked university, where platform-based collaborations and models such as micro-campuses are redefining institutional boundaries while raising new questions about power and inequality. Finally, it considers micro-credentials and digital credentialling, including blockchain-based systems, emphasising that their credibility rests on robust governance and quality assurance. Across these developments, a common theme emerges: technology does not determine educational outcomes. Its effects, whether expanding opportunity or reinforcing existing divides, depend on institutional choices, leadership, and ethical governance. The chapter concludes that the future of higher education will be shaped not primarily by technological innovation, but by the capacity of institutions and stakeholders to govern change deliberately, responsibly, and strategically.

items.title: How a Data Analytics Course in Kolkata Helps Learners Master Power BI and Business Analytics
items.abstract: Businesses today generate vast amounts of information through sales transactions, customer interactions, marketing campaigns, financial operations, websites and digital platforms. The challenge is no longer simply collecting this information. Organisations need professionals who can transform complex datasets into understandable reports, identify meaningful patterns and support business decisions with evidence. This is where Power BI and business analytics have become increasingly valuable. Microsoft Power BI enables professionals to connect data sources, transform information, build data models and create interactive dashboards that communicate business performance. Business analytics adds another layer by helping organisations interpret those findings and use them for planning and decision-making. The Growing Importance of Analytics Skills The Indian employment market is undergoing a significant technology-driven transformation. Recent reporting from the Times of India highlights that artificial intelligence is putting pressure on repetitive and outdated technology roles while increasing demand for professionals with skills in areas such as AI, data science, cloud computing and machine learning. This shift is making data-related capabilities increasingly relevant across industries. Organisations need professionals who can work with information, understand business requirements and communicate insights effectively. The demand is also visible in current hiring patterns. Recent job listings show Power BI being combined with skills such as SQL, DAX, Power Query, data modelling and ETL, demonstrating that modern business intelligence roles increasingly require a broader analytical toolkit rather than dashboard creation alone. For learners, this creates an opportunity to build a combination of technical and business skills through a data analytics course in Kolkata. Understanding the Role of Power BI Power BI is widely used for business intelligence and data visualisation. Its value comes from the ability to bring information from different sources into an environment where it can be transformed, analysed and presented. A typical Power BI workflow can involve importing information from spreadsheets or databases, cleaning the data, creating relationships between datasets, developing calculations and presenting the final results through interactive reports. This process teaches an important lesson in analytics: a dashboard is only as useful as the data and reasoning behind it. Learners need to understand the business purpose of each report, select appropriate metrics and ensure that the information presented is accurate and meaningful. A data analytics course in Kolkata can introduce learners to this complete workflow rather than treating Power BI as simply a chart-making application. Building a Strong Foundation Before Dashboard Development Effective Power BI work begins before the dashboard itself is created. Learners first need to understand data structures, data types, data quality and basic analytical concepts. Business datasets may contain duplicate records, missing values, inconsistent naming conventions or incorrect formats. Cleaning and preparing such information is therefore an essential stage of analytics. Power Query can help automate many data preparation and transformation activities. Learning these processes allows learners to create cleaner datasets before developing reports. This foundation is important because a visually attractive dashboard cannot compensate for unreliable underlying information. Developing Data Modelling Skills Data modelling is another important part of business intelligence. Organisations often have information stored across different tables and systems. Connecting these datasets correctly allows analysts to create more comprehensive reports. Learners can develop an understanding of relationships, dimensions, measures and structured data models. This helps them create reports that remain reliable as datasets become more complex. DAX, or Data Analysis Expressions, is also important for creating calculations and measures within Power BI. Developing familiarity with DAX can help learners move beyond basic visualisation towards more sophisticated analytical reporting. These capabilities are particularly relevant because current Power BI roles frequently mention DAX, Power Query, SQL, ETL and data modelling alongside dashboard development. Turning Dashboards into Business Intelligence The real value of Power BI appears when dashboards answer meaningful business needs. For example, a sales dashboard could show revenue by region, product category and month. A marketing dashboard could track campaign performance, customer acquisition and conversion rates. A financial report could monitor expenses, profitability and budget performance. However, the analyst's responsibility extends beyond displaying these metrics. The professional needs to identify unusual changes, recognise important trends and communicate their possible business significance. This is where business analytics becomes closely connected with Power BI. The technology helps present information, while analytical reasoning helps interpret it. Developing the Business Analytics Mindset Business analytics focuses on using data to understand organisational performance and support better decisions. An analyst may receive a requirement such as investigating declining sales. The solution could involve examining historical sales, customer segments, product categories, regional performance and marketing activity. The analyst may then use Power BI to visualise the findings and identify patterns. The final output should be more than a collection of charts. It should explain the evidence and highlight areas that deserve attention. This ability to connect technical analysis with business objectives is one of the most important capabilities learners can develop. Practical Projects and Real-World Application Projects provide an opportunity to combine multiple skills within one analytical workflow. A learner could work on a retail dataset and build a sales performance dashboard. items.title: HOW ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE CAN SYSTEMATICALLY ENHANCE SOFT SKILLS IN ENGLISH BLENDED LEARNING – A PEDAGOGICAL DESIGN FOR CHINESE EFL LEARNERS
items.abstract: Soft skills are essential for university students, yet many Chinese EFL learners remain at a knowledge-telling stage, prioritizing language proficiency over interpreting acquired knowledge, while curriculum design has long centered on language hard skills with soft skills often not explicitly included as instructional objectives. This marginalization of soft skills is a persistent dilemma. Artificial intelligence, especially generative AI, is profoundly reshaping foreign language education and offering new possibilities for systematically cultivating soft skills. Nevertheless, current higher education English teaching faces two separate dilemmas: the marginalization of soft skills development, and the lack of standardization in AI use. This paper focuses on the first question of how artificial intelligence tools can systematically enhance university students’ soft skills within an English blended learning environment. This paper proposes a pedagogical design aiming to transform soft skills from implicit expectations into explicit instructional objectives.

items.title: How consumers process sustainability messages in a randomized two-wave experiment on household food waste reduction in Japan
items.abstract: Abstract Information campaigns are widely used to reduce household food waste, yet little is known about how consumers process the messages they receive. This study investigates whether differently framed messages trigger qualitatively different cognitive-moral responses and whether randomized message assignment changes self-reported outcomes. In a randomized two-wave experiment with Japanese consumers (Wave 1 n = 2069; Wave 2 n = 959, five-week follow-up), participants received information framed around tax burdens (Tax frame), global hunger (Hunger frame), household monetary costs (Cost frame), or a general-information control. Open-ended responses were classified into five Norm Activation Theory (NAT; [31]) stages using two independent large language model coders with researcher adjudication, supplemented by a blinded author re-coding exercise. Framing causally shifted message interpretation: the Tax and Hunger frames increased the probability of ascribing responsibility (+ 5.1 and + 5.8 percentage points), while the Cost frame uniquely elevated personal norm activation (+ 4.5 points). However, intention-to-treat estimates show no effects on self-reported preventive practices, normative orientation, or policy support. The one persistent effect is negative: five weeks later, the Tax frame reduced food waste reduction motivation (− 0.15 SD), a pattern consistent with motivational crowding-out, although the mechanism was not directly tested. Information framing changes cognitive-moral interpretation but not self-reported practices—a process-level distinction that helps explain the intention–behavior gap and informs the design of household sustainability communication.

items.title: How to Use This Book
items.abstract: This chapter provides an instructor-oriented guide to teaching Chinese politics in an era shaped by geopolitical tension, pedagogical transformation and the growing influence of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education. It argues that teaching China today requires more than transmitting factual knowledge; it involves helping students navigate uncertainty, contested narratives, algorithmically mediated information environments and the methodological challenges of studying politics under conditions of partial visibility. The chapter outlines how the textbook&s;s modular structure, simulations, translation literacy tools, digital literacy exercises and “How Do We Know?” epistemic framework are designed to support flexible teaching across undergraduate, postgraduate and interdisciplinary contexts, while encouraging analytical reasoning, methodological reflexivity and inclusive participation. It also examines the implications of generative AI for assessment, authorship and critical thinking, arguing for pedagogical approaches that treat AI not simply as a threat to academic integrity but as an object of critical reflection and higher-order learning. In addition, the chapter situates the textbook within broader debates on inclusive curriculum design, decolonising knowledge production and diversifying perspectives in China studies, while emphasising comparative, interdisciplinary and student-centred approaches to learning. Overall, the chapter positions the study of Chinese politics as both an intellectual and pedagogical project that equips students to think critically about governance, knowledge, technology and power in an increasingly complex global environment.

items.title: HSV-Net: hybrid state-space and self-supervised vision fusion with progressive contour learning for CT pulmonary nodule segmentation
items.abstract: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed—large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space–Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset ( n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

items.title: Human Resource Development in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: A Common Good Approach
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming how and under what conditions employees learn, work, and develop their careers. This has strong implications for human resource development (HRD), because AI goes beyond technology itself and presents social and ethical issues concerning whose capabilities are recognized, whose learning is supported, and whose career futures are protected. In this paper, we develop a perspective on HRD in the era of AI through a common good lens. A common good approach to HRD not only supports employees vulnerable to job displacement by providing them with skills and mindsets beneficial for their sustainable employment and careers, but also contributes to society by developing human capital and a sustainable labor force, as well as enhancing the wellbeing of the workers and their families. This approach requires organizations to balance both efficiency and human relationships and align organizational goals (economic and social) with common good outcomes for individuals and society. It transforms HRD from a traditional HRM function into a dynamic, justice‐based, relationship‐oriented, and sustainability‐driven system. We outline several new research avenues to advance the HRD field through a common‐good lens.

items.title: Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models
items.abstract: Humans perceive far more in a scene than what is explicitly depicted: a single glance captures past causes and future trajectories; a quick peek determines if a vehicle can fit between two parked cars; a few seconds of video reveals who holds authority in a room; and a fleeting clip highlights subtle abstract patterns like unwritten rules or hidden labels. This capacity reflects a form of humanity's sixth sense: an intuitive reasoning mechanism that recovers implicit information beyond raw sensory perception. Crucially, this rapid, zero-shot visual intuition underpins everyday navigation and social interaction, making it a vital capability for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) deployed alongside people. Existing visual benchmarks, however, target either deliberate expert-level analysis in academic and mathematical domains or low-level perception, leaving the intuitive reasoning that people perform largely untested. To bridge this gap, we introduce Humanity's Sixth Sense (HSS), a benchmark for intuitive visual reasoning. HSS spans diverse image and video inputs, organizes items under a structured taxonomy, and pairs each with human-written prompts probing the implicit temporal, spatial, social, and abstract structure that people infer at a glance. Frontier MLLMs fall short of human performance: participants reach 93.1% accuracy, while the strongest model, GPT-6-astra, reaches only 53.6% even at maximum reasoning effort. Despite excelling in many complex tasks that require advanced perception and knowledge, current models still struggle significantly on these visual tasks that are intuitive for humans. We further explore agentic setup that apply dynamic visual manipulation to HSS, which narrows but does not close the gap. HSS establishes intuitive visual reasoning as a measurable axis and directs attention to a capability that scaling on current benchmarks has so far left behind.

items.title: Humanoid AI with Humanity Modeling: Bridging Humans and Virtual–Physical Humanoids
items.abstract: The seventy-year AI is now entering another major resurgence, the era of Generative AI (GenAI), characterized by the rapid advancement of large multimodal models (LMMs). GenAI and LMMs are fundamentally transforming sixty-decade-old humanoid robots, advancing them from human-looking and humanlike embodiments toward human-level AI and robotics, and inspiring a new era of AI-robotics symbiosis: humanoid AI . Humanoid AI develops humane AI-driven humanoids (AI humanoids) that go beyond traditional human-looking robots, which typically exhibit little or no humanity and intelligence due to their dedication to predefined and limited AI functions and exteriors. By contrast, AI humanoids undertake real-time, situated, and interactive mind-to-action, perception-to-behavior, and vision-to-emotion transformations, achieving an unprecedented degree of replicating human characteristics and intelligence. Realizing this vision requires systematic humanity modeling, ensuring that AI humanoids are shaped, guided, and governed by robust frameworks of AI and robotic humanity. We then propose human-virtual-physical humanoid transform and alignment and human-metaverse-humanoid ecosystem for open, complex human-digital-machine-cooperative methodology and problem-solving, followed by general principles and frameworks for building actionable humanoids and evaluating humanoid quality.

items.title: Identity Threat as a Barrier to NHS Psychology Professionals’ Adoption of Generative AI: A Technology Acceptance Model Study
items.abstract: Introduction. The development and adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) technologies is rapidly expanding, but its integration into psychological services depends on clinician acceptance. Little empirical work has examined how identity-related threat shapes psychology professionals’ adoption intentions of GenAI. The present research tested an extended technology acceptance model (TAM), with the addition of personal and professional identity threats, to explain psychology professionals’ adoption intentions of GenAI technologies for clinically relevant usage. Methods. A total of 201 UK psychology professionals completed a cross-sectional online survey. Three sequential structural equation models were tested, incorporating perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and social influence as core predictors, with threats to professional capabilities and self-threat added as extensions. Two open-ended qualitative questions were analysed using content analysis to provide broader contextual insight into current use and barriers to adoption. Results. All models demonstrated acceptable fit (CFI = 0.936–0.938; RMSEA = 0.071–0.072). Perceived usefulness emerged as the strongest correlate of adoption intention across all models (β = 0.67–0.69). Threats to professional capabilities and self-threat were each reliably negatively associated with adoption intention when entered separately, above and beyond core TAM predictors (β = −0.20 and β = −0.16 respectively). Social influence exerted a reliable indirect effect on behavioural intention through perceived usefulness across all models, as did perceived ease of use in the two models incorporating identity threat. Content analysis identified ethical concerns, lack of trust, and professional identity threats as prominent barriers to adoption. Discussion. Findings highlight the importance of considering both classic TAM factors and identity-related concerns when developing GenAI and implementing such technology into psychological services.

items.title: Image Quality Assessment in Chest Radiography According to European Guidelines: A Narrative Review of Its Relevance and Implementation Challenges in Cameroon
items.abstract: Abstract: Chest radiography remains the cornerstone of diagnostic imaging globally,functioning as a primary triage and diagnostic tool for a diverse array of cardiopulmonarypathologies, particularly tuberculosis and pneumonia. In resource-constrained environments likeCameroon, healthcare systems exhibit an extreme reliance on chest radiography; however, thestructural frameworks necessary to optimize image quality and minimize patient radiation doseare frequently inadequate. This narrative review evaluates the clinical relevance and practicalimplementation of stringent European image quality guidelines specifically the EUR 16260anatomical criteria and the European Union Directive 2013/59/Euratom within theCameroonian context. The analysis synthesizes current methods of image quality assessment,encompassing visual grading analysis, reject and repeat audits, standardized exposure indices(IEC 62494-1), and the integration of artificial intelligence tools such as CAD4TB. TranslatingEuropean standards to Cameroon encounters profound structural barriers, driven primarily by acritical shortage of radiological personnel, with a radiologist density of approximately two permillion inhabitants compared to the European average of 127 per million. Additional frictionpoints include the unmonitored transition from analogue to digital radiography, the inconsistentapplication of Diagnostic Reference Levels (DRLs), and the limited enforcement capacity of theNational Radiation Protection Agency (ANRP). Despite these systemic hurdles, strategicopportunities exist to elevate diagnostic standards. Expanding teleradiology networks to supportremote facilities, implementing low-cost quality assurance audits, and leveraging artificialintelligence for automated image assessment offer viable solutions to bridge the quality gap.The establishment of localized DRLs and the prioritized training of radiographers and medicalphysics experts stand as essential prerequisites for achieving sustainable diagnostic excellenceand radiation safety in Cameroon. Establishing routine diagnostic reference levels for standardprocedures is a universally recommended practice for adhering strictly to the ALARA principle.

items.title: Impact of AI-Based Fraud Prevention on Customer Trust in Digital Payment Systems: An Empirical Investigation of Continuance Intention among Indian Users
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of digital payment ecosystems in India, anchored by the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), has been accompanied by a sharp rise in payment fraud, eroding consumer confidence and threatening long-term adoption. Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven fraud prevention mechanisms—real-time anomaly detection, behavioural biometrics, and adaptive authentication—are increasingly deployed by payment service providers to mitigate this risk. Drawing on the Expectation-Confirmation Model of Information Systems Continuance (Bhattacherjee, 2001) and the trust literature (Mayer, Davis, & Schoorman, 1995), this study empirically examines the influence of perceived AI security features on customers' continuance intention toward digital payment applications. A cross-sectional survey of 350 active digital payment users in India was conducted using a structured, five-point Likert-scale instrument. Pearson correlation analysis revealed a very strong, positive, and statistically significant association between AI security features and continuance intention (r = .900, p < .001, 95% CI [.878, .918]). Simple linear regression confirmed that AI security features significantly predict continuance intention, explaining 76.7% of the variance (R² = .767, F(1, 348) = 1147.00, p < .001; β = .876, t = 33.87, p < .001). The findings substantiate the proposition that visible, intelligent fraud-prevention capabilities function as a salient trust-building cue, thereby reinforcing users' decision to continue using digital payment platforms. The paper discusses theoretical and managerial implications, acknowledges limitations, and outlines directions for future research.

items.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Assistance on Clinicians’ Diagnostic and Management Decisions for Indeterminate Pulmonary Nodules on CT
items.abstract: Indeterminate pulmonary nodules (IPNs) detected on computed tomography (CT) pose challenges because malignancy risk assessment is essential to balance early cancer detection with unnecessary invasive procedures. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used as a decision-support tool for pulmonary nodule assessment, but its impact on clinicians’ diagnostic and management decisions remains less established than the performance of AI algorithms. This systematic review evaluated the effect of AI assistance on clinicians’ diagnostic and management decisions for CT-detected IPNs. The review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from 2015 to 2026. Eligible studies assessed AI-assisted evaluation of indeterminate or suspicious pulmonary nodules on CT, involved clinicians, and reported diagnostic or management outcomes. Five retrospective reader-study or multireader multicase studies were included. AI assistance improved diagnostic performance and malignancy risk stratification. One study reported an AUC increase from 0.82 to 0.89 (P<0.001), with higher sensitivity, specificity, and interobserver agreement (Fleiss κ, 0.35 to 0.58; P<0.001). Another found sensitivity increased from 60% to 98% and specificity from 69% to 99%. Among advanced practice providers, AUC increased from 0.79 to 0.88, while invasive procedure recommendations for malignant nodules increased from 55% to 72%. AI detection also benefited radiologists across experience levels. Standalone AI performed worse than experienced radiologists. AI may improve clinician performance and management decisions, especially as a second-reader tool. Evidence remains limited by retrospective designs, heterogeneous systems and outcomes, and lack of randomized trials; prospective studies are needed.

items.abstract: Digital Education and Future Learning Ecosystem: Impact on Students' Academic Achievement in the 21st Century Digital Education and Future Learning Ecosystem: Impact on Students' Academic Achievement in the 21st Century In the 21st century, Education has experienced a huge paradigm shift from the traditional chalk-and-talk way of learning to technologically created learning ecosystems. The COVID-19 pandemic brought a global revolution in bringing in Digital Education. Digital India, SWAYAM, DIKSHA, PM e-VIDYA and NEP- 2020 all emphasise the role of technology in education in the Indian context. The present research paper is an effort to critically examine the impact of "Digital Education and Future Learning Ecosystem viz., e-learning platforms, Artificial Intelligence in Education (AiE) and Virtual Classrooms, on learners' academic achievement. It is primarily a descriptive and analytical study based on secondary data collected from various scholarly published papers, UNESCO reports, Reports of UGC, NEP 2020, etc. (2020-2025). The outcome of study suggested that Digital Education has a significant positive impact on Learners' Academic Achievement through personalised learning, flexibility and flexibility, accessibility, audio-visual contents and involvement, personalised learning technology and AI-based adaptive learning platforms leading to enhancement of learning outcomes by 20-30%. But the digital divide, absence of social interaction, digital fatigue and deficiency of teachers' digital skills pose challenges. The paper concludes with a suggestion that integrating both learning styles is the best sustainable future learning ecosystem for Indian Education in the context of 21st Century. The study will help all the stakeholders, viz., policymakers, educators, educational institutions etc.

Agencies now rely on online booking systems, Global Distribution Systems (GDS), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) software, artificial intelligence, digital payments, automation, and similar tools. These have made operations more efficient and improved customer service. But they have also changed things for employees: their roles, the skills they need, how much work they carry, how much independence they have, and how secure their jobs feel. items.title: IMPLICATIONS AND INSTRUCTIONAL RESPONSES TO AI-RELATED COGNITIVE OUTSOURCING IN FOREIGN LANGUAGE TEACHING
items.abstract: This article addresses the phenomenon of cognitive outsourcing in foreign language education amid the rapid proliferation of generative AI tools. Cognitive outsourcing is defined as the deliberate transfer of cognitively demanding language-learning tasks to AI systems in ways that bypass the mental processing necessary for skill development and knowledge acquisition. The study distinguishes it from legitimate uses of AI, arguing that the key criterion is whether AI involvement occurs before or after the cognitive engagement with a task. The article examines six domains in which cognitive outsourcing manifests: essay writing, vocabulary acquisition, conversational practice with AI chatbots, grammar learning, translation, and preparation for oral performance tasks. The analysis shows how AI-mediated shortcuts undermine mechanisms of second language acquisition, including generative processing in writing, productive inference in vocabulary learning, negotiation in conversation, the noticing process in grammar development, desirable difficulty in reading comprehension, and spontaneous communication in oral production. Particular attention is given to the motivational consequences of outsourcing - erosion of learners’ ideal L2 self and long-term engagement. Rejecting a prohibitionist stance toward AI as pedagogically counterproductive, the article proposes the cultivation of cognitive outsourcing awareness. This approach is presented as essential for three reasons: learners rarely recognize outsourcing dynamics without guidance; the concept offers a constructive, nonadversarial discussing AI use in the classroom; and explicit instruction addresses equity concerns, since learners with weaker metacognitive and critical literacy skills are vulnerable to uncritical AI dependence. The article concludes that fostering informed, reflective AI use offers the most viable path for preserving the developmental benefits of effortful language learning while acknowledging the realities of a technology-saturated educational environment

items.title: INFLUENCE OF AI-POWERED MARKETING ON CONSUMER ENGAGEMENT AND BRAND LOYALTY
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a working part of everyday marketing rather than a futuristic idea. Brands now use AI for personalised recommendations, chatbots, predictive analytics and automated content, and this is changing the way customers interact with them. This paper looks at how AI-powered marketing affects two closely linked outcomes: consumer engagement (how actively and how often customers interact with a brand) and brand loyalty (how likely they are to stay with a brand and keep buying from it). Since collecting fresh primary data was not possible for this paper, the study relies entirely on secondary data drawn from industry reports, survey findings published by research firms, and existing academic literature on AI and marketing. The analysis shows that AI-driven personalisation, chatbots and predictive tools generally raise engagement and can strengthen loyalty, but only when they are used with a reasonable amount of transparency and human judgement. Where AI is used carelessly, or where customers feel their data is being misused, the same tools that are meant to build loyalty can just as easily damage trust. The paper ends with practical suggestions for marketers, a note on the limitations of a secondary-data study, and directions that future researchers could explore, particularly through primary, first-hand data collection.

items.title: INOVASI PEMBELAJARAN FIQIH ERA DIGITAL: INTEGRASI ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DALAM MODEL INQUIRY LEARNING
items.abstract: Fiqh instruction in many Islamic schools remains predominantly teacher-centered, rendering it less effective for engaging the contemporary digital generation that demands active, contextual, and exploratory learning experiences. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the Inquiry Learning model offers a strategic pedagogical innovation to enhance instructional quality while maintaining the teacher's vital role as a facilitator. This study aims to describe the integration of AI across each stage of Inquiry Learning in Fiqh instruction at SMP IT Mutiara Ilmu Sokaraja, Banyumas Regency. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach with a field research design, data were gathered through classroom observations, in-depth interviews with the principal, the Fiqh teacher, and students, alongside instructional documentation review. Data analysis followed the Miles and Huberman interactive model, complemented by source and method triangulation to ensure data trustworthiness. The findings reveal that AI was systematically integrated into problem identification, data collection, data analysis, and conclusion synthesis through the utilization of ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, Google Gemini, and NotebookLM. AI was most heavily utilized during the data gathering and comparative analysis phases, while the teacher retained an indispensable role as a facilitator, ethical guide, and legal validator. These insights underscore that the successful implementation of AI in Islamic jurisprudence education relies fundamentally on the teacher's pedagogical competence to thoughtfully scaffold AI tools within an inquiry framework to cultivate critical thinking. ABSTRAK Pembelajaran Fiqih di banyak sekolah masih didominasi metode konvensional yang berpusat pada guru sehingga kurang mampu mengakomodasi karakteristik generasi digital yang membutuhkan pembelajaran aktif, kontekstual, dan berbasis eksplorasi. Integrasi Artificial Intelligence (AI) dalam model Inquiry Learning menjadi salah satu inovasi strategis yang berpotensi mentransformasi kualitas pembelajaran tanpa mengesampingkan peran guru sebagai fasilitator utama. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan integrasi AI pada setiap tahapan Inquiry Learning dalam pembelajaran Fiqih di SMP IT Mutiara Ilmu Sokaraja, Kabupaten Banyumas. Pendekatan penelitian yang digunakan adalah kualitatif deskriptif dengan jenis studi lapangan (field research). Data diperoleh melalui observasi kelas, wawancara mendalam bersama kepala sekolah, guru Fiqih, dan siswa, serta telaah dokumentasi perangkat ajar. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman, sedangkan keabsahan data diuji melalui triangulasi sumber dan triangulasi teknik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa AI diintegrasikan secara proporsional pada tahap identifikasi masalah, pengumpulan data, analisis data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dan penyajian hasil dengan memanfaatkan platform ChatGPT, Perplexity AI, Google Gemini, dan NotebookLM. Pemanfaatan AI paling dominan terdapat pada tahap pengumpulan dan analisis data, sementara guru tetap memegang kendali sentral sebagai fasilitator, pengarah etika digital, dan validator hukum syariat. Temuan ini menegaskan bahwa keberhasilan integrasi teknologi dalam pembelajaran Fiqih sangat bergantung pada kompetensi pedagogis guru dalam merajut teknologi AI secara tepat ke dalam sintaks inkuiri yang berorientasi pada nalar kritis siswa.

items.title: Institutions and Adaptation
items.abstract: This chapter examines how political institutions in China function as mechanisms of authoritarian adaptation rather than as checks on state power. It argues that the resilience of the Chinese party-state lies not in institutional liberalisation, but in the CCP&s;s ability to continuously reorganise, coordinate and recalibrate institutions in ways that preserve centralised political control while responding pragmatically to social, economic and geopolitical pressures. Using a political-technology “stack” lens, the chapter analyses how governance operates across interacting layers of discourse, bureaucracy, data, platforms and coercion, demonstrating that authority in China emerges from the coordinated functioning of an integrated party-state system rather than from isolated institutions. It explores key institutional arenas, including the National People&s;s Congress, the Two Sessions, the People&s;s Liberation Army, civil society governance and economic reform, highlighting how mechanisms such as consultative authoritarianism, stability maintenance, party-led military control and selective incorporation of NGOs contribute to regime durability. The chapter also traces the historical evolution of institutional adaptation from the reform era to the Xi Jinping period, examining how market reforms, Special Economic Zones and “socialism with Chinese characteristics” enabled economic transformation without political liberalisation. Through simulations, artificial intelligence (AI) check exercises and comparative analysis, the chapter encourages students to critically assess how authoritarian systems evolve, manage participation and sustain legitimacy under conditions of rapid social change and global uncertainty.

items.title: INTEGRATIVE MODEL FOR DEVELOPING PROFESSIONAL ENGLISH COMPETENCE OF FUTURE LAWYERS IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of higher education and legal practice, together with the internationalization of legal services and the growing integration of artificial intelligence into professional activities, have fundamentally reshaped the requirements for preparing future lawyers. In this context, professional English competence extends beyond language proficiency to encompass the ability to operate effectively in multilingual, technology-enhanced, and intercultural legal environments. The purpose of the study is to theoretically develop and substantiate an integrative model to foster the professional English competence of future lawyers through Legal English in digitally enhanced legal education. The proposed model is grounded in competency-based, communicative, interdisciplinary, and learner-centred approaches while incorporating digital pedagogy, AI-supported learning, and professional legal communication. The study employs theoretical methods, including comparative analysis, conceptual synthesis, modelling, and systematization of contemporary ESP approaches. Particular attention is devoted to authentic legal discourse, casebased learning, Moot Court simulations, digital legal resources, and generative artificial intelligence as tools that support professional language development, academic integrity, and the critical evaluation of AI-generated content. The scientific novelty lies in the development of an integrative pedagogical model that conceptualizes professional English competence as a multidimensional construction comprising motivational-professional, legal-linguistic, professional-communicative, digital-AI, and reflectivedevelopmental components. The model positions Legal English as a strategic instrument for developing professional communication, legal reasoning, digital competence, and international professional mobility. The practical significance of the model lies in its applicability to curriculum design, Legal English syllabi, ESP course development, digital learning environments and professional training for future lawyers. It also supports alignment with international professional requirements and preparation for Legal English assessment frameworks such as TOLES.

items.title: Intelligent Concrete: AI-Driven Design and Optimization of Reinforced Concrete Structures
items.abstract: Traditional reinforced concrete (RC) design has historically relied on time-consuming, iterative manual calculations to ensure structural safety. While effective for maintaining security, this method often hampers efficiency and innovation. Consequently, it has struggled to fully meet modern demands for sustainable and optimized construction. These approaches rely heavily on conservative assumptions, standardized material properties, and empirical rules. As a result, they lead to time-intensive design cycles, over-reinforced sections, and suboptimal outcomes in complex or non-standard scenarios. The inherent limitations in exploring high-dimensional design spaces and integrating multi-objective criteria (e.g., cost, durability, and environmental impact) restrict the potential for performance-based, adaptive, and resource-efficient structures. This chapter introduces artificial intelligence (AI)-driven design and optimization as a transformative paradigm shift. With the help of machine learning (ML), deep neural networks, genetic algorithms, and hybrid computational frameworks, it enables data-driven, predictive, and highly optimized RC systems. By automating generative design, topology optimization, and lifecycle performance forecasting, AI produces intelligent concrete structures that are stronger, lighter, and more sustainable. Despite its promise, the chapter also reviews key challenges such as data scarcity, interpretability of AI models, computational costs, regulatory compliance, and ethical concerns, underscoring the need for explainable AI and human–AI collaboration. Real-world case studies and meta-analyses highlight measurable environmental and economic benefits, advocating AI as a transformative paradigm for future sustainable construction. The chapter closes by calling for interdisciplinary efforts to advance reliable, transparent, and equitable AI adoption in structural engineering.

items.title: Interactive Governance for Autonomous Financial Agents: A Separation-of-Powers Architecture for AI-Driven Portfolio Execution
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence systems evolve from analytical tools into autonomous agents capable of interacting directly with financial markets, a new governance problem emerges: the same system may generate an investment decision, determine whether its own risk is acceptable, and execute the resulting transaction. This paper introduces Interactive Governance, a separation-of-powers architecture for autonomous financial agents built around a simple principle: AI can propose. Governance can authorize. Execution can execute. No component should control all three. The framework separates three distinct authorities: investment decision-making, independent authorization, and brokerage execution. It is implemented and examined through ALEX, an experimental autonomous investment architecture combining a transparent portfolio decision engine with an independently deployed execution system connected to Interactive Brokers. The implementation includes physical separation between decision and execution environments, target-state portfolio reconciliation, up to 18 deterministic pre-trade governance checks, fail-closed defaults, protocol locking, audit preservation, execution-state controls, market-session validation, liquidity and concentration limits, and independent human emergency authority. The paper also examines evidence from the ALEX Fund pilot, including unsuccessful investment outcomes, not as evidence of superior investment performance but as an empirical motivation for separating investment conviction from final risk authority. Interactive Governance is positioned as the action layer of the broader ALEX cognitive architecture, extending governance from belief formation and uncertainty management into external financial action. The resulting framework distinguishes between cognitive autonomy and operational authority and argues that increasingly capable AI systems require stronger, rather than weaker, separation between reasoning, authorization, and execution. The central conclusion is that the primary challenge in autonomous finance is no longer enabling AI to trade. items.title: KedgeFlow A Programmable Control Plane for Consequential AI Agents
items.abstract: KedgeFlow specifies a programmable control plane for admitting, authorizing, enforcing, and reconciling consequential agent actions. Its formal description, a Distributed Epistemic Admission and Transaction Control Fabric, means that policy, time-bounded evidence, multi-writer coordination, and conserved authority govern protected effects. Nine logical components and six interfaces connect existing agent harnesses to these responsibilities. The deployment profile binds user authorization, SPIFFE workloads, and DPoP proof keys; exchanges target credentials after claim; and defines cryptographic human review, Consequential Tool Descriptors, and hierarchical saga budgets. Negotiated MCP/A2A extensions connect existing workflows. Cedar, etcd, and durable workflow engines provide reusable substrates. Resource guarantees remain scoped to actual predicates and completion boundaries. Complete schemas and bounded reference implementations accompany the specification; Local deployment and staged adoption are defined through explicit acceptance gates; production conformance and industry ratification remain separate requirements.

items.title: KRISHI AI an AI and IoT-Enabled Smart Agricultural Decision Support and Equipment Management System
items.abstract: Agriculture is one of the most important sectors, which supports the economy and the livelihood of a large population. However, there are various challenges that farmers have to deal with such as choosing the right crop to grow, plant disease, varying weather conditions and agricultural equipment affordability. Small-scale farmers might have little or no capacity to buy expensive farm equipment due to its high purchasing costs and subsequent maintenance costs. The problem to be solved by the proposed paper is to develop KRISHI AI (Agri Tech system) that offers smart equipment rental through an AI and IoT enabled platform. The proposed solution will integrate artificial intelligence, machine learning, web technologies, and Internet of Things to offer a smart farming solution. The system will offer crop recommendation based on agricultural parameters, plant disease identification from images, agricultural weather-related information and rental service for farm equipment. The IoT component will be used to track equipment-related information and help manage the equipment. The web portal will offer a farmer-friendly interface where farmers can get the required services. The proposed solution will solve the problem of agricultural equipment by reducing the cost of ownership, enhance decision-making, ensure timely agricultural activities and promote the use of technology in farming.

items.title: KWSSWS-IA Approach: An Intelligent Assistant for Scientific PDF Retrieval Using Semantic Analysis and AI-Driven Summarization
items.abstract: In the age of excessive information, traditional web search engines frequently fall short in providing accurate, contextually relevant results for scientific research. Furthermore, in addition to metadata-based retrieval, this study presents an enhanced version of the Keyword Search System on Web Searching (KWSSWS), which has evolved into an Intelligent Assistant (KWSSWS-IA) capable of deep semantic analysis of full-text PDF documents. The proposed system uses transformer-based artificial intelligence (AI) models related to natural language processing (NLP) to obtain and analyze internal document components, including title, abstract, keywords, and conclusions. It automatically generates brief, accurate summaries which is associated with ranks results according to scientific relevance rather than keyword frequency, in addition to recognizing significant scientific entities like authors, publication year, journal, and domain-specific terms KWSSWS-IA presents the following results on a single screen: download link, AI-generated summary, keyword match supplied by the user, publication year, title, and authors, and source journal. Therefore, ordinary search interfaces just offer hyperlinks. Experimental evaluation reveals significant improvements in precision, recall, and utilizer efficiency compared to standard Google Scholar searches. In addition, researchers who remain short on time and seeking high-quality, domain-relevant literature may find the strategy particularly useful.

items.title: L'impact de l'intelligence artificielle sur le contrôle interne et la gestion des risques : opportunités, défis et recommandations
items.abstract: Résumé L’intégration de l’intelligence artificielle (IA) dans le contrôle interne constitue un levier stratégique de modernisation des dispositifs de surveillance et de gestion des risques, cette dernière suscite un intérêt croissant, tant dans la littérature académique que dans la pratique professionnelle. En mobilisant l’apprentissage automatique, l’intelligence artificielle (IA) transforme profondément le paysage du contrôle interne et de la gestion des risques au sein des organisations. L’IA permet d’automatiser la détection des anomalies, d’anticiper les fraudes et d’optimiser la conformité réglementaire par une analyse continue de données massives. Notre recherche repose sur une revue systématique de la littérature conduite selon le protocole PRISMA. Cette contribution s’appuie sur une revue de littérature scientifique et professionnelle afin d’évaluer les apports concrets de l’IA aux fonctions de contrôle interne et la gestion des risques afin de proposer des recommandations pratiques pour atténuer les risques tout en maximisant les bénéfices. Mots clés : Intelligence artificielle, contrôle interne, gestion des risques, digitalisation. Abstract Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into internal control serves as a strategic lever for modernizing monitoring and risk management systems an area attracting growing interest in both academic literature and professional practice. By leveraging machine learning, AI is profoundly transforming the landscape of internal control and risk management within organizations. AI enables the automation of anomaly detection, fraud anticipation, and the optimization of regulatory compliance through the continuous analysis of big data. Our research is based on a systematic literature review conducted in accordance with the PRISMA protocol. This study draws on a review of scientific and professional literature to evaluate the tangible contributions of AI to internal control and risk management functions, aiming to offer practical recommendations for mitigating risks while maximizing benefits. items.title: LANGUAGE, POWER, AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MODERN MEDIA
items.abstract: Summary. In today’s digital world, language is no longer shaped solely by human authors but increasingly by artificial intelligence (AI) systems. While these technologies enhance communication and efficiency, they also raise concerns about manipulation, bias, and misinformation. Media plays a pivotal role in shaping how information is interpreted through strategic use of language and framing. This article explores how AI-generated content and media narratives together influence modern discourse, affect public perception, and raise critical ethical questions. By examining real-life examples and theoretical insights, the paper highlights the urgent need to develop critical media and AI literacy in educational systems. This is essential to equip citizens with tools to analyze, question, and resist linguistic manipulation in an increasingly digital society. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Media Framing, Discourse, Critical Literacy, Manipulation

items.title: LAW AT THE GREEN–DIGITAL FRONTIER: Reimagining Ecological Justice, Sustainability, Economics and Technology in Emerging Environmental Governance
items.abstract: Environmental governance is changing fast. Problems in the natural world keep growing. At the same time, money needs and new technology are moving ahead. Law is now pulled into this mix more than before. This work looks at a new area where environmental rules meet digital tools. In this space, environmental law is not only about traditional regulation but it also touches sustainability goals, fairness for affected communities, trade-offs tied to the economy, and fresh technology methods. The paper reviews how economic ideas help with sustainable development. It looks at the polluter pays principle, methods for valuing the environment, carbon markets, green finance, and ways to push environmental costs back onto those who cause harm. It then turns to new tools that are starting to matter. This includes artificial intelligence, remote sensing, satellite-based monitoring, blockchain, and systems that use environmental data to guide decisions. These tools may help with compliance checks, better tracking, clearer reporting, and more solid climate choices. It mentions the risk of bias in algorithms. It discusses who controls environmental data and how rules can be enforced fairly. It notes that new technology may not reach everyone in the same way. The paper puts ecological justice first. It also highlights fairness between generations. It stresses environmental rights and the concerns of people who are often left out. Purely legal changes may not be enough. Economic tools alone will fall short. Even technology by itself will not solve the whole issue. Instead, the paper calls for one joined approach. In that view, law, the economy, ecology, and technology must connect and work at the same time. It then looks at new legal areas that could support fresh ideas. The goal is to encourage change without harming nature. It also aims to protect fair distribution and long-term sustainability. In the end, the paper imagines a legal system that can respond as things shift. It would guide both the green transition and the digital transition. At the same time, it keeps human rights, environmental protection, and accountability as key parts.

items.title: Leading with happiness in AI-driven transformation: a qualitative study of happiness-based leadership and employee well-being
items.abstract: Purpose The study aims to examine how leaders who explicitly embrace happiness and well-being as core values practice leadership during the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). It investigates how such happiness-based leaders interpret and enact their roles and how employees experience these practices in terms of motivation, trust, psychological safety and mental health. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a qualitative, interpretivist design grounded in abductive logic, the study draws on narrative interviews with top, middle and frontline leaders, complemented by semi-structured interviews and focus groups with employees across four organizations undergoing active AI implementation. Observations of town halls, change workshops and team interactions further inform the analysis. Combining narrative and thematic analysis enables interpretation of both leaders’ meaning-making stories and their enacted micro-practices in daily AI-related work contexts. Findings The study develops the concept of happiness-based digital leadership as a multidimensional configuration of practices comprising: (1) meaning-framing of AI, linking technology to organizational purpose and human values; (2) emotional containment, acknowledging fear and fatigue while modelling realistic optimism; (3) inclusive involvement, embedding participation and ethical safeguards in AI-related decisions; and (4) boundary work, protecting time, workload and human decision zones within AI governance. Three distinct leadership regimes – deep, rhetorical and instrumental – are identified, differing in the degree to which happiness practices are authentically integrated into AI governance or deployed as compliance mechanisms. Deep happiness-based digital leadership sustains trust, psychological safety and well-being; rhetorical and instrumental regimes risk turning happiness discourse into a soft form of technocratic control. Originality/value This research extends happiness management and positive leadership scholarship into AI-intensive contexts, explicating how happiness management principles can be enacted at the leadership level in AI governance. It offers conceptual and empirical insights into the emotional, ethical and governance dimensions of digital transformation, introduces a theoretically grounded typology of happiness-based leadership regimes and enriches understanding of psychological safety and emotional climate during technological change.

items.title: LLM-derived narrative metrics in chronic pain: convergent validity and novel cognitive constructs
items.abstract: The use of subjective reports and questionnaires to evaluate chronic pain, while the gold standard, conveys a limited scope of the patients’ experience and is burdensome. Here we demonstrate that large language models (LLMs) can evaluate patient-provided texts and automatically generate specific, clinically meaningful, and reliable scores for the sensory, affective, and social dimensions of chronic pain. LLMs can also generate assessor-dependent constructs such as agency and personal narrative.
